title: Stocks Got Rocked. Bonds Picked Up Some Slack
summary:
Stocks Got Rocked. Bonds Picked Up Some Slack 

             
             
            Chipmakers and other tech names got absolutely rocked today starting at the 9:30am NYSE open. Hedge funds dumped semiconductors like a bad habit early and often (Sandisk down 20% anyone?!), and with tech comprising so much of the 2026 growth story, the rest of the stock market followed suit. Bonds were a hair weaker at 9:30am, but that rapidly changed due to the magnitude of the equity market exodus. Still, 10yr yields falling a mere 5-6bps is pretty underwhelming considering stocks had their worst day in over a year and hit their worst levels since April (NASDAQ specifically). Friday's jobs report is still a contender for volatility although any major swings in stocks should set the tone.

title: Another Decent Drop as Mortgage Rates Move Under 7.2%
summary: Yesterday, it was a drop below 7.25%. Today, the 7.20% floor was broken. Mortgage rates have been on a tear over the past month and are now back to 7.17% for the average lender.  If there's one thing that deserves most of the credit for this bull run, it's the extreme bearishness in tech stocks. The NASDAQ is now down roughly 14% from the October highs and the drop perfectly coincides with the drop in bond yields and interest rates.   The road ahead is fairly simple: if tech continues causing panic in stocks, interest rates can continue to benefit. The caveat is that the benefit to rates has been getting smaller and smaller relative to the drama in stocks. This would also suggest that any miraculous bounce in stocks would likely prompt a similar correction in rates.   Economic data still matters as well. On that note, tomorrow brings the monthly jobs report, which should always be respected as a potential source of volatility.

title: HFA, Broker, AI Appraisal Review, LO Directing, AI Title Search Tools; STRATMOR on M&A
summary: Why am I a sucker for stories like, “What Do the Twins in the Shining Look Like Now?”? Is the American public a sucker for not being more concerned that no politician seems concerned about the burgeoning deficit? Will there be any “fiscal conservatives” in Congress, or the White House? Here in Dallas, one of the topics, of course, is the election. Yesterday stocks rallied and rates both dropped, reminding us that they don’t have a consistent inverse relationship, mostly on removing the uncertainty about the election. Where do we go with reducing regulatory burdens for credit-worthy borrowers, a mandate for the CFPB, FHA/VA, or banking regulators? What might happen to TRID, RESPA, Truth in Lending, or ATR? Will ink signature requirements go away? Perhaps. What about credit and appraisal policies? Will we see an expanded role for Federal Home Loan Banks? Lots of questions for a Thursday; see below for the MBA’s communication plan. (Today’s podcast can be found here. title: Modestly Weaker For a Few Potential Reasons
summary:
Bonds are starting the day a few bps weaker. 10yr yields are just over 4.90% and considering they were almost 50bps higher a month ago, you're free to go about your business today without scrutinizing this morning's baby bump. It could be purely incidental. But for those who demand scapegoats, the easiest suspect to blame would be corporate debt issuance from Apple, which coincided with bonds breaking away from their overnight stock market correlation. 
  
 In the bigger picture, we could consider investors might wonder if the NASDAQ just had another summer-sized correction and might now find support. 
  
 Lastly, we might consider the bond market correction has similarly covered enough ground as to merit a bit of cooling.  All of that is speculative, of course. If stocks resume tanking or if the econ data gets bad, the good times could easily resume. But if stocks move back toward all-time highs and the data improves, it would make sense for the recent bull run in bonds to find resistance here.

title: Redfin: Homebuyers Gain Leverage, But Pending Sales Keep Sliding
summary: Home prices are falling. Mortgage payments are easing. Sellers are becoming more willing to negotiate. Yet the housing market keeps losing buyers.Pending home sales fell 16.4% year over year during the four weeks ending Nov. 1, reaching their lowest level in Redfin's weekly records dating to 2021. Sales also slipped 0.6% from the previous four-week period, according to the brokerage's latest housing market report, released Thursday.

title: Gateway Taps ICE For Servicing Overhaul After $2.4B MSR Sale
summary: Gateway Mortgage is moving its servicing operations onto Intercontinental Exchange's (ICE) MSP platform, a technology investment that follows the lender's disclosure earlier this year that regulatory capital requirements had forced it to sell billions of dollars in mortgage servicing rights.The Jenks, Oklahoma-based lender, a division of Gateway First Bank, announced Wednesday that it will implement ICE's MSP servicing system alongside digital borrower engagement, customer service, and portfolio analytics tools.

title: Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac Purchase Originations Fall As Overall Volume Rises
summary: Mortgage purchase lending picked up in the second quarter, but Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac were notable exceptions.Purchase originations increased 7.1% year over year to approximately 1.16 million loans, according to TransUnion's Q3 2026 Mortgage Credit Industry Insights Report. Yet Fannie- and Freddie-related purchase originations declined, while other loan categories tracked by the credit reporting company posted gains.
